In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gut microbiota from healthy individuals is highly diverse, with the predominance of the polysaccharides-degrading populations and the predominant butyrates-producing species.
the intestinal microbiota of healthy volunteers is characterized by a high degree of functional diversity, which is reflected in the metabolic diversity of the microbiota.

, in the healthy human gut, there is a core group of functional microorganisms that appear to be essential for optimal fermentation and host nutrition, while other functional microorganisms are present only to a minor extent and may vary in their numbers between individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intestinal microbiota of healthy humans is characterized by a high metabolic diversity, with a predominance of the functional groups responsible for the breakdown of dietary and endogenous substratesthe most readily available carbon sources in the gut.

the intestinal microbial ecosystem of healthy humans can be characterized by the presence of a core microbiota, which is present in all individuals and is responsible for the fermentation of dietary components, and a variable microbiota, which may be responsible for the interindividual differences in the composition of the intestinal microbiome.

the human intestinal microbiota is a complex ecosystem, with a high diversity of microorganisms, and the functional groups of these bacteria are present at rather similar numbers, suggesting that the metabolic diversity of the gut microbiota is crucial for optimal fermentation and host health.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, although the gut microbial communities are diverse, the numbers of the principal fermentative groups of microorganisms are rather similar among healthy volunteers, which suggests that the gut microbial communities have a high degree of functional stability.

, in healthy individuals, a relatively small group of microorganisms, mainly belonging to the Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes phyla, appears to dominate the intestinal microbiota, and these groups of microorganisms are likely to be responsible for most of the fermentative processes occurring in the human gut.
the human gut microbiota can be considered as an ecosystem in which the different functional bacterial groups interact to maintain optimal conditions for fermentation.
